Writing base heights through ue_run_phases.py on those lines is safe: it uses the Water read, not the base read.

signature: writing a target height straight into editLayer:"Water" -> lake bed at sea level and a square pit at the write rectangle's edge
summary: Writing a target height itself into the additive Water layer counts the base twice and drags every vertex in the written rectangle toward raw 0: a lake bed at sea level and a square pit where written vertices meet untouched ones (Lake_1, T-0049). Fixed in carve_lake_bank.
source_span: Writing the target height itself into the Water layer counts the base twice and drags the whole written rectangle towards raw 0
constraints: If only the Water layer is bad: ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --carve-only --clear-water-first.
editor.undo() did not reach this: a level reload cuts the undo history, and the Water plugin's own landscape brush recompute is not a transaction.

signature: lake drawn as a flat square plane, lower than or apart from the creek -> a sunken rectangle of terrain under it, not WaterZone registration
summary: A lake's water tiles reach a little past its circle and the ground normally hides that. When the carve rectangle sinks below the water (Lake_3 and Lake_4: 20 m+, vertical walls) the tiles show as a stepped square. Fix the terrain; rebuilding the WaterZone or recreating the lake cannot.
source_span: A lake drawn as a flat square plane, lower than or apart from the creek, is a sunken rectangle of terrain under it.
constraints: Detect with ue_lake_check.py (sea_clamp, seam).
The WaterZone was healthy: level.get_water_state listed all four lakes. rebuild_water_zone reported stable/updated:false, as it always does.
Deleting and recreating the lake seemed to fix it once; that was a coincidence.

signature: carve_lake_bank "0 of N vertices changed" -> run ue_lake_check.py, do not assume the bed is clean
summary: The carve keeps any vertex already below its target, so a bed already pulled to raw 0 by an old bad write reports 0 changed and stays broken. Lake_3 and Lake_4 looked like natural cliffs this way. Verify with ue_lake_check.py.
source_span: A carve that reports "0 of N vertices changed" is not proof of a clean bed.
constraints: Signs of a broken bed: many vertices at exactly raw 0 in a blob the size of the carve rectangle, and vertical steps at its border.

signature: sunken lake bed -> restore base from a pre-lake heights png inside the carve rectangle (Water neutral), then carve again
summary: When the base terrain under a lake sank, restore base from a heights png fetched before the lake work, only inside the carve rectangle and only where it differs by more than 1 m, with the Water layer neutral; back up every vertex first, then carve again.
source_span: restore the base from a heights png fetched before the lake work, only inside the carve rectangle and only where it differs by more than 1 m, with the Water layer neutral there; then carve again.
constraints: This repaired Lake_3 and Lake_4 from the 2026-11-17 17:43 heightmap: 0 raw-0 vertices afterwards, change outside the bank at most 98 cm and 11 cm.
Do not restore from base reads taken after the damage: a restore from 11:17 base snapshots wrote the pits back.
Keep every fetched heights png with its fingerprint; it is the only reliable backup (autosaves could not be loaded remotely).

signature: ue_lake_check.py --lake LABEL,X,Y,WATER_Z,RADIUS_CM [--lake ...] [--lakes FILE] [--bank-cm 350] [--pad 2] [--json] [--project FILE]
summary: Read-only health check of a lake bed over the exact carve rectangle plus a margin, from the merged read. Findings (exit 1): sea_clamp, water_outside_ring, seam, dry_inside, missing_actor. Warnings: layer_read_mismatch, deep_inside. Run after every lake carve or repair.
source_span: Check every lake with `tools/rig-ue-mcp/ue_lake_check.py` (read-only)
constraints: seam compares the step across the carve rectangle's border with the steps just outside it, so a steep natural hillside is not reported.
It does not judge the water surface (spill, material); capture that with ue_viewport_shot.py --around.
--lakes FILE: json list of {label, x, y, water_z, radius_cm}.

signature: ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --label L --center-x X --center-y Y --water-z Z --radius-cm R --material M [--old-label Lake_<n>] [--carve-only | --materials-only | --recreate] [--clear-water-first] [--no-carve] [--delete-old]
summary: Places or reuses a WaterBodyLake: circle spline, materials, bAffectsLandscape false, move_actor to the water Z, carve_lake_bank, rebuild WaterZone, save. --carve-only repairs only the bed; --clear-water-first neutral-clears its Water layer first; --recreate places a fresh actor.
source_span: When only the Water layer is bad, `ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --carve-only --clear-water-first` writes 32768 over the carve rectangle's Water layer, carves again and saves without touching the water body.
constraints: Use --material /Game/ZAS/Water/MI_ZAS_River.MI_ZAS_River (the creek's look) unless the owner asks otherwise (lake-material-match-creek).
bAffectsLandscape is set false on purpose: true fires the Water plugin's own landscape brush on rebuild_water_zone, which fights the manual carve.
Keep the spline a uniform circle; fit the shore on the landscape with the carve.
After it: ue_lake_check.py, then ue_viewport_shot.py --around; --delete-old only after the captures look right.

--materials-only: materials and properties only (no spline rewrite, no move_actor, no carve), plus --old-label hide/--delete-old, rebuild and save; used live 2026-11-18 to switch all four lakes to MI_ZAS_River and delete the old discs.

signature: base-layer height calls next to carved lakes, applied without Water compensation -> carved beds sink again in every rewritten tile
summary: unreal_lake_smooth.py (and every terrain helper) writes visible heights into the base Layer and rewrites whole 127-vertex tiles. Two runs next to Lake_3 did this while the lakes' Water offsets were in place, so the carved beds in those tiles sank again.
source_span: Two smoothing runs next to Lake_3 (09:01 and 09:06) wrote visible heights into the base `Layer` while the Water layer still held the lakes' carve offsets, so every carved vertex in those tiles sank by its offset again.
constraints: Fixed at the root: ue_run_phases.py now subtracts the Water offset (ue-run-phases-water-compensation). Still run ue_lake_check.py before smoothing next to a lake.
Keep the fingerprinted heights png from before any terrain run: it is what the repair uses (lake-bed-repair-from-reference-heights).

signature: landscape.set_height_region without editLayer over a carved bed -> apply only through ue_run_phases.py (writes base = height - (water - 32768))
summary: Terrain helpers emit visible heights into the base Layer. Over a carved lake the Water offset was applied twice, sinking the bed in every rewritten tile. ue_run_phases.py now reads the Water layer per call and subtracts the offset.
source_span: Before each such call `ue_run_phases.py` now reads the Water layer of the same tile and writes base = height - (water - 32768), so a carved lake bed inside a rewritten tile is not carved a second time.
constraints: Never apply a height calls json any other way (e.g. replaying it with ue_route.py call): the compensation lives only in ue_run_phases.py.
--no-water-compensation is only for a calls json that really holds base-layer heights.
A failed Water read stops the run before the write (rerun with --start N).

signature: lake water showing past its circle near a creek mouth -> original ground there is below the lake surface; lower the water Z or raise a rim
summary: Where the ground beyond the bank is below the lake surface (Lake_4 west: 7217 against water 8798; Lake_3 north/east: 8168 against 8860), the water shows past the circle. The carve only lowers ground, so lower the lake's water Z to its rim or raise a rim except where the creek enters.
source_span: The carve only lowers ground, so it cannot fix this: lower the lake's water height to its rim or creek-mouth level, or raise a rim except where the creek enters.
constraints: The owner chose rims (2026-11-18): built with unreal_water_berms.py along every creek and around every lake (water-shows-past-its-shape).

signature: ue_viewport_shot.py OUT.png --around X Y Z RADIUS
summary: Captures the owner's current view unmoved, then top, east, north, west, south, close-low and far views of the subject to OUT_<view>.png, then puts the owner's camera back. Exit 1 if any view failed; the others are still written.
source_span: Use `ue_viewport_shot.py OUT.png --around X Y WATER_Z RADIUS_CM`: it captures the owner's current view first
constraints: Judge water, carves and placement from several angles and distances: one angle showed a broken Lake_3 as a clean round lake.
The image comes back inline over the normal uemcp route; the scp pull from the migrate account is only a fallback.
Without --camera or --around it captures the current view without moving it (use that when the owner says not to move the camera).

signature: level.set_editor_visibility {hidden:true} -> sets bHiddenEdTemporary, not saved; the actor shows again after any level reload
summary: set_editor_visibility only sets the temporary editor flag, which is not saved: after an autosave was opened and closed, the old Lake_<n> discs showed again as a flat glassy surface over Lake_1 and Lake_2. Re-hide after every reload, or delete the actor once approved.
source_span: `level.set_editor_visibility {hidden:true}` only sets the temporary editor flag (`bHiddenEdTemporary`), which is not saved
constraints: ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --old-label re-hides on every run; --delete-old removes the disc once the owner approves the lake.
A forced reload has also wiped a cylinder's OverrideMaterials.
level.load to another map often reports a timeout although it worked: read level.get_current before retrying.
All four old Lake_<n> discs were deleted on 2026-11-18 (ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --materials-only --old-label Lake_<n> --delete-old).

signature: WaterBodyLake WaterMaterial -> /Game/ZAS/Water/MI_ZAS_River.MI_ZAS_River (the creek's material)
summary: Lake_1 and Lake_2 use MI_ZAS_River (translucent, rippled, the creek's own look); MI_ZAS_Lake renders flat, opaque and glassy. Give every lake the creek's material unless the owner asks otherwise.
source_span: Lake_1 and Lake_2 use `/Game/ZAS/Water/MI_ZAS_River.MI_ZAS_River` (translucent, rippled, the creek's own look); `MI_ZAS_Lake` renders flat, opaque and glassy.
constraints: Switch one lake: level.set_water_body_property {actorLabel, propertyName: WaterMaterial, value: MI_ZAS_River path}, then level.save.
Owner confirmed 2026-11-18 ("creek water is better"); all four lakes now use MI_ZAS_River. Switch an existing lake with ue_lake_as_waterbody.py --materials-only.

signature: unreal_water_berms.py --heights live.png --water water.json --out berm_calls.json --out-heights berm.png [--report R] [--crest-cm 60] [--crest-m 24] [--slope 0.5] [--max-raise-m 20] [--project FILE]
summary: Plans berms along every creek and around every lake: a crest of water level + 60 cm for 24 m outside the water edge, then a 0.5 slope down to the ground. Only raises; never inside any water body or on ground below the sea. Apply with ue_run_phases.py only.
source_span: It only raises ground, never inside any water body (so creek mouths, junctions and lake outlets stay open), never on ground below the sea, and caps each raise at `--max-raise-m` (20)
constraints: A lake's berm starts past its carved bank, so the carve's underwater shore stays as it is.
Exit 1 when a raise was capped: the report lists those points; lower that body's water level there instead.
Render the planned raise over the terrain before applying (berm-never-on-sea-floor).
After applying: level.save, fetch heights and compare with --out-heights, ue_lake_check.py --lakes, ue_viewport_shot.py --around, then ue_creek_foliage.py over every creek and lake.
Live 2026-11-18: 871 vertices raised over 4 creeks and 3 lakes, highest 10.3 m, none capped; live heights equal to the plan.

signature: tools/rig-ue-mcp/ue_water_fetch.py --out water.json [--project FILE]
summary: Read-only: writes every WaterBodyRiver (spline points with water level, RiverWidth per point from WaterSplineMetadata), every WaterBodyLake (centre, radius, water level from its circle spline) and the sea level into one json, the --water input of unreal_water_berms.py.
source_span: `tools/rig-ue-mcp/ue_water_fetch.py --out water.json` (read-only)
constraints: Its `lakes` list is also a valid ue_lake_check.py --lakes file.
RiverWidth is read with editor.get_property on <river actor path>.WaterSplineMetadata (level has no get_component_property).

signature: creek or lake water visible past its spline/circle -> the ground just outside is below the water; build berms
summary: The Water plugin draws each body a little past its shape (ShapeDilation 4096 cm, 24 m mesh tiles) and the ground hides that. Where the ground just outside is below the water, the water shows as a stepped sheet past the shape. A carve only lowers ground; berms raise it.
source_span: the Water plugin draws it a little past its shape (each body's `ShapeDilation` is 4096 cm here and the water mesh tiles are 24 m)
constraints: Fix with ue_water_fetch.py + unreal_water_berms.py, or lower that body's water level.
A whole sunken carve rectangle under a lake shows the same way as a square plane: that is lake-square-plane-is-sunken-terrain, check with ue_lake_check.py first.

signature: berm plan near a creek's sea mouth -> never raise ground below the sea level
summary: The first live berm plan built a 13 m berm out into the ocean around Creek_2's mouth, because the creek's last stretch was a few cm above the sea. unreal_water_berms.py now never raises ground below the sea level; always render a plan before applying it.
source_span: The first live plan built a 13 m berm out into the ocean around Creek_2's mouth, because the creek's last stretch was a few cm above the sea
constraints: Creek samples within 5 cm of the sea level get no berm either.

signature: foliage.add_instances with thousands of transforms in one call -> bridge timeout and editor crash; send batches of about 200
summary: foliage.add_instances crashed the rig's editor on EVERY call on 2026-11-18 (any batch size, type, mode or level). Cause (T-0061, 2026-11-19): the experimental MeshPartitionWater plugin; it is disabled as code (project_plugins.json).
source_span: re-added 2031 in one `foliage.add_instances` call: the bridge timed out after 30 s and the editor crashed inside `AddFoliageInstances`
constraints: Before any foliage-adding --apply, run tools/rig-ue-mcp/rig_project_plugins.py (dry run): it must report that the rig matches project_plugins.json.
Python InstancedFoliageActor.add_instances crashed the same way, so it is no workaround when the plugin is on.
Still send large re-adds in batches (--add-batch 200) and write the removal receipt first.

signature: ue_look_check.py --from-calls atmo.json [--from-calls ...] | [--checks FILE] [--level-path PATH] [--project FILE]
summary: Read-only check of the level's look against the recipe that worked: star dome material, sun and sky light, post-process values and their override flags, leaf Contrast/SS Power. Exits 1 on drift. Run after any editor crash, restart or level.load, before judging colour work.
source_span: the star dome had lost its `MI_Star_Nebula_02` override and was drawing a dynamic instance of its base `M_Star_Nebula` (no cubemap), which is black
constraints: A black sky makes auto exposure brighten the whole scene: leaves wash out to pale mint with every leaf value still right.
A post-process value is ignored unless its Settings.bOverride_<Name> flag is true; check the flag, not just the value.
Restore the dome with the single OverrideMaterials call; rerunning all of unreal_sky.py also resets the sun and sky light.
--from-calls turns every value an applied calls json set into a check and resolves actors by label: the generic form for any game; the plain defaults are the test game's object names.

signature: unreal_atmosphere.py --out atmo.json --project game.json [--dome ''] [--exposure E] [--no-atmosphere] [--no-clouds] [--cloud-coverage 0.35] [--no-fog] [--fog-density 0.01]
summary: Writes the phases that tame a too-bright scene under the nebula dome: locked exposure, dimmer nebula (MI Power), weak SkyAtmosphere, low volumetric cloud layer with a project MI, light height fog, then the dome override and save LAST. Apply with ue_run_phases.py; check with ue_look_check.py.
source_span: writes all of it as phases (exposure, nebula, atmosphere, clouds, fog, then the dome override and `level.save` LAST)
constraints: Any game: labels from the profile label_prefix (or post_process_label, sun_label, sky_dome_label), cloud MI under content_root/Sky, fog at sea_cm.
No nebula dome: sky_dome_label "" or --dome '' (no nebula/dome calls; atmosphere haze 1.0).
Exposure is per game: measure with ue_look_probe.py --sweep-exposure; 0.45 fits the test game only.
Idempotent (onConflict skip); verify with ue_look_check.py --from-calls atmo.json.

signature: PostProcessVolume auto exposure pinned at its minimum
summary: A scene that looks too bright may be auto exposure sitting at its brightest allowed value in every view, not pumping. Locking Min = Max at the floor gave identical captures. Lock it at a darker value (higher = darker); set it with level.set_post_process_settings enableOverrides.
source_span: The PostProcessVolume's auto exposure range was 0.3..2.5 and it sat at 0.3, its brightest end, in every view
constraints: Exposure bias is logarithmic: -0.7 was far too dark.
level.set_component_property cannot reach post-process settings (they are on the actor).

signature: MI_Star_Nebula_* Power / Power_Extra_Cubemap
summary: On the star-dome nebula material, Power is an exponent: lowering it makes the sky BRIGHTER (0.4 blew out 71% of the sun-side sky, 1.4 only 18%). Dim the nebula by raising Power on the MI asset.
source_span: The nebula `Power` is an exponent: LOWER IS BRIGHTER.
constraints: Never use the dome blueprint's Brightness variables instead (see dome-construction-script-drops-nebula).

signature: BP_Star_Dome variables / level.move_actor on the dome
summary: Setting a BP_Star_Dome variable or moving the dome reruns its construction script, which replaces the MI_Star_Nebula override with a dynamic instance of the black base material: the sky goes black and auto exposure washes the scene out. Change the MI asset instead and restore the override last.
source_span: replaced the `MI_Star_Nebula_02` override with `MID_M_Star_Nebula_0`, a dynamic instance of the black base material
constraints: Restore with level.bulk_set_component_property OverrideMaterials (unreal_sky.py's call).
ue_look_check.py flags it.

signature: VolumetricCloud under a custom sky dome
summary: A VolumetricCloud alone renders flat and grey, and its default 5 km layer hides behind a 20 km sky dome near the horizon. Add a SkyAtmosphere (AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale ~0.35 keeps a nebula dome visible) and lower the layer to ~1 km.
source_span: A `VolumetricCloud` alone rendered (seen looking straight up) but flat and grey
constraints: Cloud coverage: Cloud_GlobalCoverage on a project MI of m_SimpleVolumetricCloud_Inst (engine default -0.2).
Ground cloud shadows did not appear on the test level even with bCastCloudShadows (open item).

signature: ue_look_probe.py --out-dir DIR [--at X Y Z] [--yaws 0 90 180 270] [--pitch -8] [--sweep-exposure E ... --post-process LABEL] [--target 105]
summary: Measures how bright a level looks: captures the owner's view plus horizon views, prints ground mean luminance and sky clipping; with --sweep-exposure locks each exposure value in turn, restores the original settings and camera, and names the value closest to --target.
source_span: captures the owner's view and four horizon views per value, prints the ground and sky numbers, restores the original exposure and the camera
constraints: Nothing is saved; the original Min/Max exposure and their override flags are restored.
Sun-facing views read darker (backlit); judge on the others and look at the pictures.
Put the chosen value in the profile's exposure key for unreal_atmosphere.py.
